about: Offline Hood holder-exit contracts from exact merged source. Every address, amount, hash and time is made up; times are days before or after one made-up instant. api-source rows are Candle's own pure deriveHolderExit run on made-up chain facts at one block, in the read route's envelope (the route, the chain read and its cache are not run). api-stub rows are response stubs for the agent route (a dry run, a completed exit, a partial and an indeterminate one, a refusal), shaped by the SDK's types and the route's refusal table; the route, the builder and the signer are not run. mcp, sdk and cli rows read the same answers through the registered tools, the SDK and `candle token exit <token>` over an intercepted fetch: nothing is sent, signed or read from a chain. portfolio-marks-source and docs rows are the source's own text, read as text; `candle portfolio` itself is not run. No deployed behavior is claimed.

outcome.message: holderExit() requires an apiKey: pass one in CandleClientOptions (new CandleClient({ apiKey }))

outcome.text: | `token exit <token> [--wallet <0x address\|main>] [--recover [--amount <tokens>] \| --enter-recovery \| --claim-team] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--json]` | Hood only. Where a holder of a Candle Hood launch stands if it does not migrate: the state (none, awaiting migration, Recovery can be opened, Recovery, rescue pending, rescued), the API's one-sentence disclosure printed verbatim, when Recovery opens (the creator after 7 days, anyone after 30), the fixed Recovery rate and what is left, any rescue request, the team vesting escrow, and for the wallet its balance, what Recovery would pay it and the actions it may take now. The read needs no key; the wallet is `--wallet`, else the account's embedded Hood wallet when a key is selected. `--recover` (approves the exact `--amount`, default all, then redeems), `--enter-recovery` and `--claim-team` run that action through Candle with the embedded Hood wallet (`swap:write` for the Recovery actions, `launch:write` for `--claim-team`): the API's dry run is shown first, then the CLI asks, or takes `--yes`; `--dry-run` stops after it and sends nothing. There is no destination: Recovery pays the wallet that redeems and a team claim always pays the escrow's recipient. A refusal prints the API's code beside the disclosure. Exit codes: 0 done, 1 refused or partial (the approval landed and the claim did not: run it again), 3 indeterminate (a call was sent and its result is not known yet: read again before running it again), 5 you declined the prompt and nothing was sent. `candle portfolio` marks Hood positions whose launch is in Recovery, has a pending rescue or was rescued, and points at this command. |

| `candle_holder_exit` | `GET /api/v1/hood/curves/:curve/holder-exit` (with `token`, `GET /api/v1/markets/hood/:token` first): where a holder of a Candle Hood launch stands if it does not migrate: state, Recovery window and fixed rate, any rescue request, the team vesting escrow, and with `account` that wallet's balance, Recovery payout and the actions it may take now. Give `curve` or `token`; quote `holderExit.disclosure` verbatim | No |

| `candle_claim_holder_exit` | `POST /api/v1/agent/hood/holder-exit/:curve`: one Hood holder exit for the account's wallet: `enter_recovery`, `claim_recovery` (approves the exact amount, then redeems) or `claim_team` (always pays the escrow's recipient). Candle signs with the embedded Hood wallet; `dryRun` defaults to true; no destination argument | Yes (`swap:write`; `launch:write` for `claim_team`) |

Release 0.6.28 (BE-3794), with CLI 0.13.34 and MCP 0.10.39. Hood holder exits (BE-3630 design section 6): `MarketState.holderExit` (type `HolderExit`, optional; absent on an older API) says where a holder stands if a Hood launch does not migrate: `state` (`none`, `awaiting_migration`, `recovery_open`, `recovery`, `rescue_pending`, `rescued`), the Recovery window, the fixed rate and progress, any rescue request, the team vesting escrow, the `actions` that would succeed now, and `disclosure`, one sentence to show verbatim; `holderExitUnavailable: true` when that read failed. `getHolderExit(curve, account?)` and `getHolderExits(account)` read it per curve and per account, with no key. `buildHolderExit({ curve, account, action, amountRaw? })` returns the unsigned calls for the holder's own wallet (no key; nothing signed) and `recordHolderExit({ curve, account, txHash })` records a sent one. `holderExit({ curve, action, amountRaw?, dryRun?, wallet?, linkedSigning? })` runs it on an agent key (Candle signs with the embedded Hood wallet; a linked wallet gets `signing[]` for `submitHolderExit`), with the fee claim's per-call `not_sent` / `submitted_unknown` / `confirmed` / `reverted` and a sequence `outcome`. Every refusal from these routes is a `HolderExitError` (a `CandleApiError`) with the API's code, `details`, and for a sequence that did not complete `outcome`, `calls` and `warnings`. No request has a destination field and the SDK encodes no calldata. MCP adds `candle_holder_exit` and `candle_claim_holder_exit` (`dryRun` defaults to true) and quotes the holder-exit disclosure on `candle_get_market`; the CLI adds `candle token exit <token>` (`--recover`, `--enter-recovery`, `--claim-team`, `--dry-run`) and `candle portfolio` marks Hood positions with an open exit.
